newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah slides on pre-poll jitters.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah slides on pre-poll jitters.

text.p: * Indonesian rupiah falls ahead of campaign launch for May election. Stop-loss and options-related dollar buying add to rupiah weakness.
* Malaysian ringgit hit by long liquidation after failing to strengthen beyond 2.4950/dollar but sentiment still upbeat.
* Thai baht falls on dollar short-covering, activity slow ahead of key economic data.
* Singapore dollar confined to stale range as ringgit/Sing interest fades.
The Indonesian rupiah took centre-stage among Southeast currencies on Thursday as players sold the unit amid growing nervousness ahead of the country's general elections on May 29.
Dealers said the market was anxious about possible unrest during the pre-poll campaign, beginning on Sunday.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,428.75/29.75 at 0415 GMT, around its morning low, against an opening of 2,420.5/21.5.
A Japanese bank dealer in Jakarta said a relatively ample rupiah market helped the dollar buying. Overnight money was traded at 10.0 percent in the morning.
He said the small dollar rally was launched by Singapore operators and some local players followed.
"Most of the dollar buying is options-related and stop-loss orders being triggered," said a European bank dealer in Singapore.
He said the dollar had breached several technical and psychological barriers against the rupiah and looked set for the next target of 2,430.0.
"Jakarta corporates are selling (the dollar). But there's buying from interbank players and funds," he said.

Bank Indonesia's inaction in the face of the rupiah's slide was contributing to the market's bullish stance on the dollar, he said, but added that interbank players were becoming uneasy about pushing the dollar higher.
A Singapore-based economist said the rupiah's weakness was temporary and the currency would recover once the market's focus returned to economic fundamentals after the election.
In Malaysia, the ringgit fell back below the 2.5000 level against the dollar as funds liquidated their long positions after the currency failed to strengthen beyond 2.4950.
Dealers said sentiment remained positive on the ringgit due to high Malaysian interest rates and a strong economy.
They said the market was awaiting Malaysia's February trade data, due in a few days. A modest surplus is widely expected.
"The big picture for dollar/ringgit is still down in the medium-term but we have to break 2.4940 convincingly to resume the trend," the European bank dealer in Singapore said.

Malaysian interest rates have been firming over the last two weeks partly due to a withdrawal of funds by foreigners from both deposits and the stock market and partly due to new paper issues from the central bank.
"There are several arbitrage opportunities, which people are exploiting now, particularly in the short-tenors," a swaps dealer with a Malaysian bank said.
The Thai baht came under pressure from some dollar short-covering but dealers said activity was subdued ahead of the release of key economic data in the afternoon.
The baht was quoted at 26.077/26.080 to the dollar at 0415 GMT against 26.068/26.073 late on Wednesday. The central bank set the mid-rate at 26.07 per dollar versus 26.08 on Wednesday.
"There was some normal dollar demand ahead of the month-end. But the overall trading volume remained light," a foreign bank dealer in Bangkok said.
The Singapore dollar was trapped in a tight range as the recent spate of buying in the ringgit/Sing cross dwindled, leaving the domestic unit without much momentum.
Dealers said the Sing dollar was likely to remain in the same 1.4420-1.4460 range to the U.S. dollar seen on Wednesday. It was quoted at 1.4435/45 at 0415 GMT.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
